name: Multi-select
purpose: Choose several values from a fixed list and keep them visible. The field holds a filtering input; the list stays open while choices are made; each choice appears as a removable chip. Use it for statement accounts, filter facets, recipients — anywhere the answer is a set rather than a value.
$provenance-note: NEW at #203 (wave 3b, lane J) against itinerary row 22 (P2, 'Chips-in-field selection'). Verified absent first-hand: ls knowledge/snippets/ | grep -i multi → only Chart-combo/other unrelated names; no multi-select meta; grep -rn 'aria-multiselectable' knowledge/snippets/ → 0 hits. The gated Dropdown META lists a 'multi-select (non-native)' VARIANT, but its snippet implements single-select only (its own header says 'CANONICAL REFERENCE for the non-native single-select Dropdown'), so the variant was documented and never built.

props.name: display
props.$status: PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed. Both are built. Chips-in-field keeps every choice visible but grows the field; count-summary keeps the field one row tall and moves the chips beneath it. Which is the default is a design decision, not this lane's to rule.

props.name: state
props.$note: Same state channel as Input-fields/Textarea — inherited, not re-specified.

props.name: max
props.$note: Optional ceiling on the number of selections. Not exercised in the reference — the limit story is demonstrated on Tags-input, where free entry makes it load-bearing.

variants.name: chips-in-field
variants.use: Every selection visible and individually removable; the field wraps and grows.

variants.name: count-summary
variants.use: The field states the count and stays one row tall, so dense forms and toolbars do not reflow as choices are made.

tokens.field-border: form/border/default; focus-within form/border/active + a 4px inset bottom stroke; disabled form/border/disabled; error a 4px inset rag/error stroke (dark: full rag/error border)
tokens.chip: INHERITED FROM TAGS — 1px form/border/default on a transparent fill, border-radius/control (square in Mono), label text/default, dismiss glyph icon/default. No new chip tokens are introduced.
tokens.option-highlight: form/background/hover fill PLUS a 3px inset rule in form/border/active — never colour-alone
tokens.hit-area: target/min (44px) on the field row, the disclosure toggle and every option row. The chip dismiss button is 24px — the gated Tags value, inherited unchanged.

accessibility.roles: input[role=combobox] + aria-autocomplete="list" + aria-expanded + aria-controls; popup role=listbox with aria-multiselectable="true" and role=option children carrying aria-selected. Highlight via aria-activedescendant — focus never leaves the input.
accessibility.keyboard: Down opens; Up/Down move the highlight; Enter toggles the highlighted option WITHOUT closing; Escape closes; Backspace on an empty input removes the last selection. Each chip's dismiss button is in the tab order.
accessibility.announcements: A polite live region announces the selection count after every change, because the visual chip appears outside the reading order of the user's current position.
accessibility.states: Disabled and error exposed programmatically (disabled, aria-invalid + aria-describedby). The error message pairs a symbol with words and stays ink.
accessibility.targetArea: Field row, toggle and option rows 44px. Chip dismiss 24px (WCAG 2.5.8 minimum) — inherited from Tags, flagged rather than silently raised.

antiPatterns: Closing the list after each choice. The whole point is picking several without re-opening.
Drawing a second chip. The chip is the gated Tags chip; if it changes, it changes in Tags first.
Confusing this chip with the Selection-controls chip. That one is a toggle the user presses directly; this one is a receipt of a choice made in the list, and removal is its only interaction.
Leaving the selection count unannounced — a chip added below the caret is invisible to a screen-reader user.
Silently truncating the chip row. If the field must stay one row tall, use the count-summary variant, which says how many are chosen, rather than hiding choices.
